newsitem.title: Singapore: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah down on liquidity, holiday.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah down on liquidity, holiday.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah weakens on ample liquidity and underlying concerns about election campaign.
* Malaysian ringgit in narrow range ahead Labour Day holiday, seen weakening on month-end dollar demand.
* Singapore dollar's upside limited by U.S. dollar buying interest.
* Thai baht edges up but good two-way interest seen.
The Indonesian rupiah lost its footing again on Wednesday as ample money market liquidity and underlying concerns about the general election campaign triggered dollar buying.
"It's mainly the liquidity which is driving the dollar up," a local bank dealer in Jakarta said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,433.25/33.75 at 0440 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,426.50/27.50.
A dealer in Singapore said a public holiday there on Thursday also sparked off a spate of dollar short covering.
"People here don't want to go home with open positions."
"I think it's also mainly liquidity driven. If people were pulling out from short dollar outright positions, forwards would have also been taken," the dealer said.

"The trading pattern now is that before a holiday or the weekend, people will go long dollars because of the election. But after the holiday, if nothing happens, they'll start selling them back," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said the dollar could face some resistance around 2,435.0/38.0.

In Malaysia, the ringgit was stuck in a narrow range as activity dwindled ahead of the Labour Day holiday, but dealers said it could come under pressure from month-end dollar demand and continued selling by international funds.
"The market is also waiting for the Malaysian cabinet's reaction to the Singapore newspaper report about Johor," a Singapore-based analyst said.
The Singapore Straits Times ran a report on Tuesday saying Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew was probably justified in criticising Malaysia's southern Johor state.
On Tuesday, a Singapore court agreed to expunge from a legal affidavit Lee's remark that Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
"If there is a strong reaction from the Malaysian cabinet, there should be a selloff in both Sing and ringgit," the analyst said.
Dealers said the ringgit and Singapore dollar were also being driven by activity in the ringgit/Sing cross, which has seen choppy trading in recent days.
"The funds are just playing it. I don't think there's any fundamental reason to buy or sell ringgit/Sing at this point," the U.S. bank dealer said.
He said dollar/Sing was still within its 1.4420-1.4480 range and was unlikely to weaken below 1.4400 as there was strong buying interest all the way down from 1.4440.
In Thailand, the baht firmed to around 26.115/26.119 at 0440 GMT against 26.125/26.130 late on Tuesday.
But dealers said buying of the dollar, on expectations it would head higher against the majors, was restricting the Thai currency's upside.
"The liquidity remained very high today. There was no incentive to hold the baht right now as (baht) short-term interest rates are pretty low," a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok said.
Rising liquidity pushed the overnight interbank rate down to 6.50-7.00 percent in early morning trade from 7.25-7.50 percent late on Tuesday.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
